exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Tower, Cathay 251, holding point Runway 07 Right on Alpha, ready for departure.
exchanges.meaning: The pilot reports holding short at the holding point and ready to depart; 'departure' is used because the word 'takeoff' is forbidden until ATC issues the clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, Hong Kong Tower, Runway 07 Right, line up and wait.
exchanges.meaning: ATC authorizes Cathay 251 to taxi into position on the runway and align with the centerline; throttles remain at idle — this is not permission to roll.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Runway 07 Right, line up and wait, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: Standard readback of the line-up authorization.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, wind 080 degrees, 14 knots, Runway 07 Right, cleared for takeoff.
exchanges.meaning: The takeoff clearance with wind information, authorizing Cathay 251 to begin the high-speed departure roll.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Runway 07 Right, cleared for takeoff, Cathay 251.
exchanges.meaning: Standard readback of the takeoff clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, Runway 07 Right, line up and wait.
exchanges.meaning: The canonical short form of the line-up authorization: enter the runway, align with the centerline, keep throttles at idle — no permission to roll.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, cancel takeoff clearance, hold position.
exchanges.meaning: The command cancelling a takeoff clearance before the roll starts; the aircraft must remain in position.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.meaning: The emergency abort command used after the takeoff roll has started; the crew must stop the aircraft immediately.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.meaning: The pilot's readback confirming the emergency stop.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, STOP IMMEDIATELY! Cancel takeoff clearance, vehicle on the runway!
exchanges.meaning: The tactical drill's emergency abort: the takeoff clearance is cancelled because an inspection vehicle is on the runway.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay 251, NEGATIVE! HOLD POSITION, line up and wait ONLY.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory ATC correction after a hearback error where the pilot read back 'cleared for takeoff' instead of 'line up and wait'.

vocabulary.definition: Authorization to taxi into position on the active runway and align with the centerline; throttles stay at idle and the aircraft must not roll until cleared for takeoff.
The takeoff clearance authorizing the aircraft to begin the high-speed departure roll; the word 'takeoff' is only issued by ATC as a clearance or cancellation.
The ICAO rule that the word 'takeoff' is strictly reserved for the actual takeoff clearance or its cancellation — pilots report ready with 'ready for departure', never 'ready for takeoff'.
An emergency stop initiated on the runway before reaching V1: throttles closed, maximum braking, speedbrakes and maximum reverse thrust until the aircraft halts.
Takeoff decision speed — the maximum speed at which the takeoff can still be rejected and the aircraft stopped on the remaining runway; above V1 the takeoff must continue.
An instruction to remain stopped and not move the aircraft.

quiz.question: [Question 1 — Air Law & Radiotelephony (ICAO Doc 9432)] When holding short of an active runway and completing before-takeoff checks, what is the correct ICAO phraseology to notify the tower that you are ready?
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO Doc 9432, the word 'TAKEOFF' is strictly prohibited when reporting ready — pilots must always say 'ready for DEPARTURE' so the word cannot be misheard as an actual takeoff clearance.

quiz.question: [Question 2 — Principles of Flight & Performance (V-Speeds)] What is the operational significance of V1 speed during a takeoff roll?
options: It is the speed at which the pilot pulls back on the control yoke to rotate the aircraft.
It is the maximum speed at which the pilot can reject the takeoff and bring the aircraft to a safe stop within the remaining runway length.
It is the best rate of climb speed with one engine inoperative.
It is the maximum flap extension speed.
quiz.explanation: V1 is the Takeoff Decision Speed — above V1, stopping within the available runway is no longer possible, so the takeoff must be continued even after a catastrophic failure.

sections.heading: Core Learning Content — Takeoff Phraseology
sections.body: Per ICAO Doc 9432: (1) Report ready as "Hong Kong Tower, Cathay 251, holding point Runway 07 Right on Alpha, ready for departure." — NEVER say "ready for takeoff"; the word "takeoff" is taboo until ATC uses it in the clearance. (2) Line up: ATC "Cathay 251, Runway 07 Right, line up and wait." → readback "Runway 07 Right, line up and wait, Cathay 251." Meaning: taxi onto the runway, align with centerline, throttles at IDLE — NO permission to roll. (3) Takeoff clearance: ATC "Cathay 251, wind 080 degrees, 14 knots, Runway 07 Right, cleared for takeoff." → readback "Runway 07 Right, cleared for takeoff, Cathay 251." (4) Cancelling: before the roll starts — "Cathay 251, cancel takeoff clearance, hold position."; after the roll starts — "Cathay 251, STOP IMMEDIATELY!" → readback "Stopping, Cathay 251."

sections.heading: Spaced Repetition (Forgetting Curve) Review
sections.body: Day 6 & 8 recall — (1) Conditional clearance readback: condition first, action, repeat condition (e.g. "Behind landing B777, line up Runway 07R behind"). (2) If ATC gives a conditional line-up but the crew cannot see the landing traffic, report "Negative contact, holding short" — never enter on assumption. (3) Signage mnemonics: "Black square, you're there!" (location sign), "Yellow array, points the way!" (direction sign), "Red and white, runway in sight!" (mandatory stop sign).

sections.heading: Fun Aviation Fact Of The Day
sections.body: V1, the "point of no return": before every departure, pilots calculate V1 (decision speed), Vr (rotation speed), and V2 (single-engine climb speed). Below V1, if an engine fails or ATC aborts, the pilot can safely stop on the remaining runway; above V1 the aircraft CANNOT stop on the runway — even if an engine explodes or catches fire, the pilot MUST continue the takeoff, get airborne, and deal with the emergency in the air.
